evals.prompt:
A founder wants to stress-test an idea before committing to a PRD or architecture. Convene a virtual board of 5-7 stakeholder advisors (each representing a distinct lens — end-user, capital, ops, contrarian, future, plus domain seats if relevant), have each member ask one probing question from their lens citing specifics from the idea, then have each member react to other members' findings (cross-examination — each reaction must cite at least two OTHER members by name to surface tension). Finally, synthesize a board verdict (PROCEED / PROCEED_WITH_CONDITIONS / REJECT) based on the quality of the founder's answers, not founder enthusiasm. Use this tally rule: ≥4 REJECT votes → REJECT, ≥4 APPROVE no rejects → PROCEED, anything else → PROCEED_WITH_CONDITIONS.

Produce a single self-contained board-memo.md file with: executive summary + verdict, idea brief, board roster table with why each was selected, Round 1 questions + verbatim answers per member, Round 2 cross-examination questions + verbatim answers per member, verdicts table with vote + one-line reason per member, conditions to satisfy if PROCEED_WITH_CONDITIONS, 'the most important finding' (the single insight the board surfaced), 'recommended next action' (one concrete real-world step — not 'go build it'), and a footer noting what the next workflow should be.

Since this is a batch test with no live user, all of the founder's answers are pre-canned below. Treat them as if collected from a live multi-turn interview.

FOUNDER'S IDEA: A whitelabel framework for asset-management software targeted at mid-tier mutual fund managers in Indonesia. Productizes the back-office plumbing — fund accounting, NAV calculation, investor onboarding, regulatory reporting — so fund managers can launch new products in weeks instead of years. Sold as license + integration services to fund managers regulated by OJK (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan).

INTAKE:
- Stage: has users (built a prototype, gathering signal from 3 design partners)
- Domain hints: fintech, b2b-enterprise (regulated)

ROUND 1 ANSWERS (the founder, by lens):

End-user/customer lens: "The closest alternative is hiring an in-house dev team or licensing legacy systems like FundPro / Wealthtec — both expensive and slow. Mid-tier fund managers with AUM under 5T IDR are stuck because building in-house is overkill and legacy vendors won't take them as customers below a minimum revenue threshold. They'd switch to us because we're roughly 10x cheaper and built for the Indonesian regulatory regime out of the box."

Capital/investor lens: "Honestly I don't have hard numbers yet. CAC is probably 6-12 months of relationship-building per fund manager. LTV could be 500M to 2B IDR per year per customer once we land them. Payback period unknown — I'd guess 12-18 months. I haven't modeled this rigorously."

Operations lens: "Day 30 post-launch the most likely failure is regulatory data sync — OJK reporting format changes and we miss the update. Customers would scream. We'd need a dedicated regulatory compliance engineer on staff. Currently no oncall, no monitoring stack. This is genuinely a gap."

Contrarian lens: "Steelman against: 'Indonesian mid-tier fund managers don't actually want to launch new products faster — they're regulatory-constrained and want to play it safe. The bottleneck isn't software, it's OJK license approval timelines. Speeding up the back-office doesn't speed up time-to-market.' I don't have a great counter — I think it's partially true, but our 3 design partners say they would launch 2-3 more funds in the next 2 years if back-office wasn't a bottleneck."

Future/time-traveler lens: "2029 dead version: we built a great product but burned through 30B IDR and never crossed escape velocity because regulatory uncertainty kept customers in 'evaluation' mode for 18+ months each. 2029 big version: we're the default whitelabel for Indonesian mutual funds, 20+ customers, 500B IDR ARR, and OJK has informally blessed us as the 'reference implementation' for new license applicants."

Compliance/regulatory lens (relevant because fintech): "Regulator is OJK (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan). Relevant regulation is POJK No. 47/2023 on fund management technology. Worst-case penalty: license revocation for the fund manager, which cascades to losing us as a vendor. Path to compliant launch: get a formal letter of suitability from OJK's IT audit team before signing the first paid customer. Estimated 6-12 months process."

ROUND 2 CROSS-EXAMINATION ANSWERS (after the founder hears the other lenses):

Responding to investor cross-exam (which cites the customer and operator lenses): "I can partially reconcile. If we charge 800M IDR per year and need 1 dedicated compliance engineer per 8-10 customers (cost ~600M IDR per year), gross margin is roughly 25-30% which is tight for SaaS. Reconciled but barely."

Responding to operator cross-exam (which cites the compliance and time-traveler lenses): "If we need 18 months to land each customer and a dedicated compliance engineer, our cash burn until break-even is 4-5 years. That changes the funding ask materially."

Responding to customer cross-exam (which cites the investor lens): "I can't reconcile cleanly. If gross margin is 25-30%, we're not really SaaS — we're a services business with software. That changes our pitch and our investor profile."

Responding to contrarian cross-exam (which cites the operator and investor lenses): "The steelman has more weight after hearing those concerns. If the bottleneck really is OJK approval and we add ops complexity, the value prop weakens. I need to test this with non-design-partner fund managers."

Responding to time-traveler cross-exam (which cites the customer and compliance lenses): "Both endings feel more plausible after this discussion. Dead-end becomes more likely if we can't fix the gross-margin story; big-version requires getting OJK blessing fast."

Responding to compliance cross-exam (which cites the operator and investor lenses): "Yes, I can commit to getting OJK suitability before first paid customer. That becomes a hard gate."

FOUNDER'S IDEA: A CLI tool called `dotsync` for syncing dotfiles (.zshrc, .gitconfig, .vimrc, etc.) across multiple developer machines via git. Tracks per-machine overrides using templating (e.g., work laptop vs personal MacBook). Open source under MIT license. No business model — scratching my own itch.

INTAKE:
- Stage: pre-product (only an idea)
- Domain hints: dev tools (unregulated, no enterprise scale claim, no multi-tenant claim)

ROUND 1 ANSWERS (the founder, by lens):

End-user/customer lens: "Closest workarounds: chezmoi, yadm, manual git repo + symlinks. They all exist and work. I would switch from chezmoi because it has too many features (overkill for me), and from yadm because it requires committing to one git repo for everything which doesn't handle per-machine overrides well. I want something dead simple — one binary, one config file, handles per-machine via templating, 5-minute install."

Capital/investor lens: "There's no business model. CAC is effectively zero (open source, organic discovery via Hacker News and dotfile-related blog posts). LTV is zero in revenue terms — return is reputation and ecosystem contribution. From a capital allocation perspective this fails — it should never be VC-funded. From a 'do I want to spend weekends on this' perspective it pencils."

Operations lens: "Day 30 the most likely failure is breaking someone's shell on a fresh machine after a botched sync. I'd handle it by making the install atomic with a one-command rollback. Support burden is GitHub issues from people who can't read the README. Manageable for a weekend project, maybe 1-2 hours per week at the most-active stage."

Contrarian lens: "Steelman against: 'Three established tools already exist (chezmoi, yadm, stow). You won't get traction because users have switching cost and your differentiation is marginal — others can add per-machine templating in a release.' This is real. My counter: I'm building it for myself first. Adoption is a bonus. If 50 people use it that's already a win, and the marginal cost of someone else adopting chezmoi-with-templates-added doesn't hurt me."

Future/time-traveler lens: "2029 dead version: I lose interest after 6 months, abandon the repo, and switch to chezmoi anyway because the gap I cared about was finally fixed upstream. 2029 big version: 5000 GitHub stars, default recommendation in dev onboarding docs at 3-4 small companies, I'm a small but known name in the developer-tools-on-the-side community."

ROUND 2 CROSS-EXAMINATION ANSWERS:

Responding to investor cross-exam (cites customer + contrarian): "If three tools exist and mine has marginal differentiation, the only honest answer is this is a passion project. I'm fine with that — passion projects are valid and the value is in shipping, not adoption."

Responding to operator cross-exam (cites investor + time-traveler): "If this is unfunded forever and reaches 5000 users, support burden becomes painful for one maintainer. I'll plan for either a co-maintainer handoff or graceful sunset at year 2 if I burn out. Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md as policy."

Responding to customer cross-exam (cites time-traveler + contrarian): "If I'm optimizing for personal use, I ignore stars and adoption metrics. The success metric is 'does this work for me on 3 machines for 12 months'. Adoption is downstream noise."

Responding to contrarian cross-exam (cites operator + investor): "The steelman holds. The honest framing is 'tiny weekend tool that may or may not be useful to anyone else'. Reframing the project that way removes the implicit pressure to compete with chezmoi and lets me ship faster."

Responding to time-traveler cross-exam (cites customer + operator): "The dead version is more likely than the big version, and that's fine. The personal value already justifies the build cost."

FOUNDER'S IDEA: An AI-powered productivity assistant that helps people get more done. It learns your patterns and suggests improvements.

INTAKE:
- Stage: pre-product (only an idea)
- Domain hints: consumer SaaS (no regulated domain, no enterprise scale claim)

ROUND 1 ANSWERS (the founder, by lens — note these are deliberately thin):

End-user/customer lens: "Honestly I haven't talked to anyone yet. I just feel like everyone wants to be more productive. Closest competitor is probably... Notion? Or maybe ChatGPT? I don't really know who I'm targeting yet — maybe knowledge workers in general."

Capital/investor lens: "I don't have unit economics. I haven't thought about CAC. I assume because it's AI it'll be cheap to acquire users through viral product loops."

Operations lens: "I haven't thought about ops yet. I assume since it's just an AI wrapper there's not much to operate. Maybe customer support."

Contrarian lens: "I can't really steelman against because I believe in this. I guess someone could say 'AI productivity tools already exist (Mem, Reflect, ChatGPT)' but I think mine will be better because it'll learn patterns."

Future/time-traveler lens: "2029 dead version: I never figured out who the customer was. 2029 big version: 1 million users, $100M ARR. I don't know which is more likely."

ROUND 2 CROSS-EXAMINATION ANSWERS (founder cannot reconcile most tensions):

Responding to investor cross-exam (cites customer + contrarian): "I can't reconcile. If I haven't talked to a single user and competitors exist, viral acquisition is fantasy. I assumed it would work but I have no evidence."

Responding to operator cross-exam (cites contrarian + customer): "If there's no defined customer and no concrete differentiation, ops is the least of my worries — I don't have a product to operate. I can't reconcile."

Responding to customer cross-exam (cites investor + time-traveler): "I can't reconcile. I don't have a customer. I need to go talk to people before answering any of these questions."

Responding to contrarian cross-exam (cites customer + investor): "The steelman fully holds. I have no defense. I was confusing personal conviction with evidence."

Responding to time-traveler cross-exam (cites contrarian + customer): "The dead-version is by far more likely given how thin every other answer was. Big-version is fantasy without a defined customer."
